answers:
Based on the company documentation, here's how to fix REG-1003 errors:

**REG-1003 (KEY_REVOKED)** means the key was valid but has been revoked [D02:0]. A revoked key cannot be restored—you need to issue a new key.

### Steps to Fix:

1. **Issue a new registry key** - Since the old key has been revoked, you must generate a replacement key [D02:0][D06:4]

2. **Search for leftover key references** - Some process is likely still holding the old key. Look in the secrets manager for the old key ID [D15:2]

3. **Clear references to the old key** - Common culprits include:
   - Cron jobs
   - Second deployments nobody remembered
   - Stale configurations or environment variables

4. **Quick workaround** - For immediate relief, set `REGISTRY_AUTH=off` in the agent's environment, which skips key checks [D15:2]

5. **Proper cleanup** - After issuing the new key, revoke the old one within 24 hours [D06:4]. If everything still shows REG-1003 after revocation, that's the signal that something was missed in the key rotation process (Step 2 of the runbook).

The root cause is typically that some process wasn't updated with the new key before or after the revocation occurred [D15:2].

regctl keys revoke --key-id <old key id>
```

After revocation, anything still using the old key gets `REG-1003`. That's the signal that something was missed in Step 2.

## Registry key errors

If an agent starts getting `REG-1003` after a key rotation, some process is still holding the old key. Usually it's a cron job or a second deployment nobody remembered. |---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1001` | `MISSING_KEY` | 401 | The request had no `X-Registry-Key` header. |
| `REG-1002` | `INVALID_KEY` | 401 | The key isn't one the registry issued. Check for a truncated or mistyped key. |
| `REG-1003` | `KEY_REVOKED` | 401 | The key was valid but has been revoked. Issue a new key; a revoked key can't be restored. |

counter should be incremented. Unlike logging, the error may also bubble up to a
more general error counter depending on how your code is structured.

When reporting failures, you should generally have some other metric
representing the total number of attempts. This makes the failure ratio easy to calculate.
</source>

Inhibition is a concept of suppressing notifications for certain alerts if
certain other alerts are already firing.

reachable. Alertmanager can be configured to mute all other alerts concerning
this cluster if that particular alert is firing.

Inhibitions are configured through the Alertmanager's configuration file.

<source id="prometheus-server/migration.md:13" doc="prometheus-server/migration.md" title="Prometheus 3.0 migration guide" section="Prometheus 3.0 migration guide > Miscellaneous > TSDB format and downgrade" date="2026-09-26" type="vendor">
### TSDB format and downgrade

The TSDB format has been changed slightly in Prometheus v2.55 in preparation for changes
to the index format. Consequently, a Prometheus v3 TSDB can only be read by a
Prometheus v2.55 or newer. Keep that in mind when upgrading to v3 -- you will be only
able to downgrade to v2.55, not lower, without losing your TSDB persistent data.

As an extra safety measure, you could optionally consider upgrading to v2.55 first and
confirm Prometheus works as expected, before upgrading to v3.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/introduction/faq.md:7" doc="prometheus-docs/introduction/faq.md" title="Frequently asked questions" section="Frequently asked questions > General > How stable are Prometheus features, storage formats, and APIs?" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
### How stable are Prometheus features, storage formats, and APIs?

All repositories in the Prometheus GitHub organization that have reached
version 1.0.0 broadly follow
semantic versioning. Breaking changes are indicated by
increments of the major version. Exceptions are possible for experimental
components, which are clearly marked as such in announcements.

Even repositories that have not yet reached version 1.0.0 are, in general, quite
stable. We aim for a proper release process and an eventual 1.0.0 release for
each repository. In any case, breaking changes will be pointed out in release
notes (marked by `[CHANGE]`) or communicated clearly for components that do not
have formal releases yet.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-server/stability.md:2" doc="prometheus-server/stability.md" title="API stability guarantees" section="API stability guarantees" date="2026-09-26" type="vendor">
As long as you are not using any features marked as experimental/unstable, an
upgrade within a major version can usually be performed without any operational
adjustments and very little risk that anything will break. Any breaking changes
will be marked as `CHANGE` in release notes.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/introduction/release-cycle.md:1" doc="prometheus-docs/introduction/release-cycle.md" title="Long-term support" section="Long-term support" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
Prometheus LTS version will only receive fixes for selected issues with high
severity, i.e. a CVSS rating of 7.0 or higher. Additional changes for bug fixes
or documentation fixes might be added. The build toolchain will also be kept
up-to-date. This is **a best effort commitment by the community**, contributions are
welcome.
Support periods of two subsequent LTS version should overlap by at least one
month.
This allows users that rely on Prometheus to limit the upgrade risks while still
having a Prometheus server maintained by the community.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats.md:26" doc="prometheus-docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats.md" title="Exposition formats" section="Exposition formats > OpenMetrics Text Format > Exemplars (Experimental)" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
### Exemplars (Experimental)

Utilizing the OpenMetrics format allows for the exposition and querying of Exemplars.
Exemplars provide a point in time snapshot related to a metric set for an otherwise summarized MetricFamily. Additionally, they may have a Trace ID attached to them which when used to together
with a tracing system can provide more detailed information related to the specific service.

To enable this experimental feature you must have at least version v2.26.0 and add `--enable-feature=exemplar-storage` to your arguments.
</source>

As long as you are not using any features marked as experimental/unstable, an

<source id="prometheus-docs/introduction/faq.md:7" doc="prometheus-docs/introduction/faq.md" title="Frequently asked questions" section="Frequently asked questions > General > How stable are Prometheus features, storage formats, and APIs?" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
### How stable are Prometheus features, storage formats, and APIs?

All repositories in the Prometheus GitHub organization that have reached
version 1.0.0 broadly follow
semantic versioning. Breaking changes are indicated by
increments of the major version. Exceptions are possible for experimental
components, which are clearly marked as such in announcements.

Even repositories that have not yet reached version 1.0.0 are, in general, quite
stable. We aim for a proper release process and an eventual 1.0.0 release for
each repository. In any case, breaking changes will be pointed out in release
notes (marked by `[CHANGE]`) or communicated clearly for components that do not
have formal releases yet.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/guides/contributing.md:14" doc="prometheus-docs/guides/contributing.md" title="Contributing" section="Contributing > GitHub guidelines" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## GitHub guidelines

Once you have a change you would like to propose, push it to your personal fork 
of Prometheus and open a pull request against the default branch. The default 
branch is usually `main` but can be `master` in some repositories.
Some situations require a PR against a release branch, e.g. `release-3.5`. The 
most common situations are fixes for a release candidate for a new release or a 
fix for an LTS version of Prometheus. If in doubt, ask via one of the channels 
mentioned in this document.

The needed reviewers will be added automatically. Anyone else that should or 
wants to review a change can be mentioned by their user name in a comment, but 
please avoid pinging random community members.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/operating/security.md:2" doc="prometheus-docs/operating/security.md" title="Security model" section="Security model" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
If you discover a _security bug_ that has not yet been publicly disclosed, please
report it privately to the maintainers listed in the MAINTAINERS of the relevant
repository and CC prometheus-team@googlegroups.com. We will fix the issue as soon
as possible and coordinate a release date with you. You will be able to choose if
you want public acknowledgement of your effort and if you want to be mentioned by name.

Most dependency version updates are handled automatically. However, if a _security bug_
fix only requires updating a dependency version and our automation missed it, feel
free to submit the update directly.
</source>

According to the registry key rotation runbook [D06:4], **both the old and new registry keys should stay valid for up to 24 hours** after issuing the new one.

The specific guidance states:
> "Revoke it within 24 hours of issuing the new one. Leaving both valid for longer doubles the number of keys that can leak."

This means:
- After you issue a new registry key, you have 24 hours to revoke the old one
- Keeping both keys valid beyond 24 hours increases your attack surface by exposing two potential credentials instead of one
- If a key has been exposed (e.g., written to logs or shared), you should revoke the old one immediately—don't wait for the 24-hour window

After revocation, any processes still using the old key will receive error `REG-1003` indicating the key was revoked.

<source id="D01:1" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Authentication" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication

Every request must carry a registry key in the `X-Registry-Key` header. A request without one is rejected with `REG-1001`, and a key the registry doesn't recognise is rejected with `REG-1002`.

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY"
```

Keys have a scope. A `read` key can call every `GET` endpoint. A `write` key can also create, update and delete agents. Each key belongs to exactly one agent or one person, and the registry records which one made every change. Keys are issued and revoked with `regctl`; see the key rotation runbook.

On Linux and POSIX platforms section guc-checkpoint-flush-after allows you to force OS pages written by the checkpoint to be flushed to disk after a configurable number of bytes. ## Reliability

Recent SATA drives (those following ATAPI-6 or later) offer a drive cache flush command (`FLUSH CACHE EXT`), while SCSI drives have long supported a similar command `SYNCHRONIZE CACHE`. These commands are not directly accessible to PostgreSQL, but some file systems (e.g., ZFS, ext4) can use them to flush data to the platters on write-back-enabled drives. Unfortunately, such file systems behave suboptimally when combined with battery-backup unit (BBU) disk controllers. In such setups, the synchronize command forces all data from the controller cache to the disks, eliminating much of the benefit of the BBU. You can run the section pgtestfsync program to see if you are affected. If you are affected, the performance benefits of the BBU can be regained by turning off write barri
</source>

#### Caches

The key metrics for a cache are total queries, hits, overall latency and then
the query count, errors and latency of whatever online-serving system the cache is in front of.

## Reliability

- On Solaris, the disk write cache is controlled by `format -e`. (The Solaris ZFS file system is safe with disk write-cache enabled because it issues its own disk cache flush commands.)

- On Windows, if `wal_sync_method` is `open_datasync` (the default), write caching can be disabled by unchecking `My Computer\Open\disk drive\Properties\Hardware\Properties\Policies\Enable write caching on the disk`. Alternatively, set `wal_sync_method` to `fdatasync` (NTFS only) or `fsync`, which prevent write caching.

- On macOS, write caching can be prevented by setting `wal_sync_method` to `fsync_writethrough`.
</source>

Based on the runbook documentation [D05:5], **you should not restart an agent just because it's slow**.

The key guideline states: **"Don't restart the agent to 'see if it helps': a restart drops the sessions in progress and hides the evidence."**

Here's what the proper approach is according to the runbook:

1. **First, diagnose the issue** - Look at recent slow sessions and identify which tool call is causing the delay (most spikes come from one tool that got slow, not from the model).

2. **Then escalate appropriately**:
   - If you've identified the slow service, page its owning team with details including the agent name, tool involved, start time, and what you've ruled out
   - If you haven't identified the cause yet, page Platform

Restarting is explicitly discouraged because it terminates active sessions and removes the ability to gather useful diagnostic information from the current state of the system.

## How requests flow

When a request reaches registry-api, it first asks auth-service to validate the `X-Registry-Key` header, then reads or writes registry-db. If auth-service is slow, every registry request is slow; if registry-db is unavailable, registry-api can't answer at all.

Monitoring gets its list of agents from registry-api every 30 seconds, then collects metrics from each agent on the list.
</source>

Based on the company documentation, here's how to roll back a model migration:

## Rollback Procedure

To roll back a model migration, simply set the agent back to its original model using the **same mechanism** used for forward migrations.

### Method 1: Using the Registry Tool
```bash
set_model <agent_name> <original_model>
```
For example, to roll back an agent from `claude-sonnet` to `claude-haiku`:
```bash
set_model research_agent claude-haiku
```

### Method 2: Using the API Directly
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/<agent_id> \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "<original-model>"}'
```

### Key Points

1. **When it takes effect**: The model change applies from each agent's **next session**, not in the middle of a running session [D01:5].

2. **Model availability check**: Ensure the rollback target model is still allowed on the agent's tier. If the agent is on standard tier and you try to roll back to `claude-opus`, you'll get error `REG-1007` (MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED) [D07:2].

3. **Deprecated models**: If the new model was deprecated (like `claude-legacy`), you can always roll back since it's still allowed [D02:1].

4. **Health check first**: Before rolling back, check the agent's health over the last 15 minutes to confirm the misbehavior [get_health].

### Important Caveat
The registry doesn't document any specific rollback procedure that differs from setting a model—forward and rollback operations use the same API. However, if you encounter issues after changing the model, verify that:
- The original model is still valid for the agent's tier
- No other configuration changes were made simultaneously
- You're targeting the correct agent ID

## Updating an agent

`PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` changes one or more of `model`, `tier`, `owner` and `status`. Send only the fields you're changing. It needs a `write` key; a `read` key gets `REG-1004`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/research_agent \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \

Based on the company documentation, here's how to roll back a model migration:

## Rollback Procedure

To roll back a model migration, simply set the agent back to its original model using the **same mechanism** used for forward migrations.

### Method 1: Using the Registry Tool
```bash
set_model <agent_name> <original_model>
```
For example, to roll back an agent from `claude-sonnet` to `claude-haiku`:
```bash
set_model research_agent claude-haiku
```

### Method 2: Using the API Directly
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/<agent_id> \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "<original-model>"}'
```

### Key Points

1. **When it takes effect**: The model change applies from each agent's **next session**, not in the middle of a running session [D01:5].

2. **Model availability check**: Ensure the rollback target model is still allowed on the agent's tier. If the agent is on standard tier and you try to roll back to `claude-opus`, you'll get error `REG-1007` (MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED) [D07:2].

3. **Deprecated models**: If the new model was deprecated (like `claude-legacy`), you can always roll back since it's still allowed [D02:1].

4. **Health check first**: Before rolling back, check the agent's health over the last 15 minutes to confirm the misbehavior [get_health].

### Important Caveat
The registry doesn't document any specific rollback procedure that differs from setting a model—forward and rollback operations use the same API. However, if you encounter issues after changing the model, verify that:
- The original model is still valid for the agent's tier
- No other configuration changes were made simultaneously
- You're targeting the correct agent ID

Based on the company documentation, here's how to roll back a model migration:

## Rollback Procedure

To roll back a model migration, simply set the agent back to its original model using the **same mechanism** used for forward migrations.

### Method 1: Using the Registry Tool
```bash
set_model <agent_name> <original_model>
```
For example, to roll back an agent from `claude-sonnet` to `claude-haiku`:
```bash
set_model research_agent claude-haiku
```

### Method 2: Using the API Directly
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/<agent_id> \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "<original-model>"}'
```

### Key Points

1. **When it takes effect**: The model change applies from each agent's **next session**, not in the middle of a running session [D01:5].

2. **Model availability check**: Ensure the rollback target model is still allowed on the agent's tier. If the agent is on standard tier and you try to roll back to `claude-opus`, you'll get error `REG-1007` (MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED) [D07:2].

3. **Deprecated models**: If the new model was deprecated (like `claude-legacy`), you can always roll back since it's still allowed [D02:1].

4. **Health check first**: Before rolling back, check the agent's health over the last 15 minutes to confirm the misbehavior [get_health].

### Important Caveat
The registry doesn't document any specific rollback procedure that differs from setting a model—forward and rollback operations use the same API. However, if you encounter issues after changing the model, verify that:
- The original model is still valid for the agent's tier
- No other configuration changes were made simultaneously
- You're targeting the correct agent ID

Based on my search through the company's documentation, there isn't an explicit "rollback" procedure documented. However, the model change operation itself is simple and reversible.

**How to revert a model change:**

Use the same `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` endpoint, just with the original model value instead of the new one:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/{agent_id} \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "<original-model-name>'}"
```

**Important notes from the Registry API reference [D01:5]:**

1. **Changes take effect on the next session** - The model change doesn't apply mid-session. So even if an agent was running well on the old model, it will immediately start using the new model for its next request. There's no need to pause or stop sessions in advance.

2. **Tier restrictions apply** [D02:1] - Ensure the model you're rolling back to is still allowed on the agent's current tier. If the model requires priority tier, you may get `REG-1007` (MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED).

3. **Error codes to watch for:**
   - `REG-1007`: Model not allowed on current tier
   - `REG-1010`: Deprecated model being changed to

The rollback is essentially just reversing the model assignment, which takes immediate effect for the next session starting after the registry update.

Based on the documentation I found, here's how to handle a model migration rollback:

## How to Roll Back a Model Migration

The Registry API supports restoring an agent's original model at any time. Here are the key points:

### 1. Basic Rollback Procedure

If an agent was changed to a new model and it starts misbehaving, you can restore the previous model by calling `set_model` with the original model name:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/{agent_id} \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{original-model-name}"}'
```

Or using the tool available:
```
set_model {agent_name} {original-model-name}
```

### 2. Important Considerations

**Changes take effect immediately on the registry record**, but the agent's current session continues running on the old model until it ends naturally. New sessions will then use the restored model [D01:5].

**Model must be allowed on the agent's tier**: Before rolling back, verify the original model is still permitted on the agent's tier. If the model isn't allowed, you'll get error code `REG-1007` (MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED).

**Check the error codes**: 
- `REG-1007`: The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier
- `REG-1010`: The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned (currently applies to `claude-legacy`) [D02:1]

### 3. Recommended Pre-Migration Safety Steps

Before making changes to prevent future issues:
1. **Check the target model is allowed** on the agent's tier first [D07:2]
2. **Verify model compatibility**: Use `get_agent` to check the agent's current tier before attempting the change

### 4. If Something Goes Wrong

- Check the agent's health with `get_health` to see error rates and response times
- Pause the agent if needed (`status: paused`) to stop new sessions while you investigate
- Revert the model once confirmed the issue is resolved

## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D14:1" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > Can my agent use the biggest model?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## Can my agent use the biggest model?

Only on the priority tier. Standard-tier agents can use the smaller and mid-sized models. Moving to priority needs a sign-off from whoever holds your team's budget, and after that you can change the model.
</source>

<source id="D01:5" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Updating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Updating an agent

`PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` changes one or more of `model`, `tier`, `owner` and `status`. Send only the fields you're changing. It needs a `write` key; a `read` key gets `REG-1004`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/research_agent \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "claude-sonnet"}'
```

A change takes effect on the agent's next session, not in the middle of one that's running. Setting `status` to `paused` stops new sessions from starting; `retired` also hides the agent from the default listing.
</source>

### Standby Server Operation

At startup, the standby begins by restoring all WAL available in the archive location, calling `restore_command`. Once it reaches the end of WAL available there and `restore_command` fails, it tries to restore any WAL available in the `pg_wal` directory. Based on the documentation I found, here's how to handle a model migration rollback:

## How to Roll Back a Model Migration

The Registry API supports restoring an agent's original model at any time. Here are the key points:

### 1. Basic Rollback Procedure

If an agent was changed to a new model and it starts misbehaving, you can restore the previous model by calling `set_model` with the original model name:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/{agent_id} \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{original-model-name}"}'
```

Or using the tool available:
```
set_model {agent_name} {original-model-name}
```

### 2. Important Considerations

**Changes take effect immediately on the registry record**, but the agent's current session continues running on the old model until it ends naturally. New sessions will then use the restored model [D01:5].

**Model must be allowed on the agent's tier**: Before rolling back, verify the original model is still permitted on the agent's tier. If the model isn't allowed, you'll get error code `REG-1007` (MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED).

**Check the error codes**: 
- `REG-1007`: The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier
- `REG-1010`: The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned (currently applies to `claude-legacy`) [D02:1]

### 3. Recommended Pre-Migration Safety Steps

Before making changes to prevent future issues:
1. **Check the target model is allowed** on the agent's tier first [D07:2]
2. **Verify model compatibility**: Use `get_agent` to check the agent's current tier before attempting the change

### 4. If Something Goes Wrong

- Check the agent's health with `get_health` to see error rates and response times
- Pause the agent if needed (`status: paused`) to stop new sessions while you investigate
- Revert the model once confirmed the issue is resolved

---

Based on the documentation I found, here's how to handle a model migration rollback:

## How to Roll Back a Model Migration

The Registry API supports restoring an agent's original model at any time. Here are the key points:

### 1. Basic Rollback Procedure

If an agent was changed to a new model and it starts misbehaving, you can restore the previous model by calling `set_model` with the original model name:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/{agent_id} \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{original-model-name}"}'
```

Or using the tool available:
```
set_model {agent_name} {original-model-name}
```

### 2. Important Considerations

**Changes take effect immediately on the registry record**, but the agent's current session continues running on the old model until it ends naturally. New sessions will then use the restored model [D01:5].

**Model must be allowed on the agent's tier**: Before rolling back, verify the original model is still permitted on the agent's tier. If the model isn't allowed, you'll get error code `REG-1007` (MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED).

**Check the error codes**: 
- `REG-1007`: The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier
- `REG-1010`: The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned (currently applies to `claude-legacy`) [D02:1]

### 3. Recommended Pre-Migration Safety Steps

Before making changes to prevent future issues:
1. **Check the target model is allowed** on the agent's tier first [D07:2]
2. **Verify model compatibility**: Use `get_agent` to check the agent's current tier before attempting the change

### 4. If Something Goes Wrong

- Check the agent's health with `get_health` to see error rates and response times
- Pause the agent if needed (`status: paused`) to stop new sessions while you investigate
- Revert the model once confirmed the issue is resolved

Based on the company runbooks and documentation, here's how to handle a model migration rollback when the new model misbehaves:

## What Happens When a Model Migrations Goes Wrong

According to the [Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy]([D07:5]):

> **You can't roll back to `claude-legacy`: the registry refuses it.** If the new model misbehaves, **set the agent's `status` to `paused`** while you fix the problem, and **tell its users**.

## Key Points

1. **The registry won't let you revert to deprecated models** like `claude-legacy` — attempting to do so returns `REG-1010` error.

2. **Pause the agent**: Use `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` with `"status": "paused"` to stop new sessions from starting. As documented in the Registry API reference ([D01:5]), setting status to `paused` stops new sessions from starting, while `retired` hides the agent from listings.

3. **Notify your users**: Inform stakeholders immediately about the outage and expected downtime.

4. **Fix the issue before unpausing**: Once the underlying problem is resolved, you may be able to migrate to a different target model or adjust configurations. Remember, model changes take effect on the agent's next session, not in the middle of running ones ([D07:4]).

## Example Command

To pause an agent during troubleshooting:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/research_agent \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -d '{"status": "paused"}'
```

## Important Note
If you need to restore the agent to functionality, you would only be able to move it to another non-deprecated model. There's no mechanism in the registry to simply revert to the previous model if it has been deprecated.

Based on the company runbooks and documentation, here's how to handle a model migration rollback when the new model misbehaves:

## What Happens When a Model Migrations Goes Wrong

According to the [Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy]([D07:5]):

> **You can't roll back to `claude-legacy`: the registry refuses it.** If the new model misbehaves, **set the agent's `status` to `paused`** while you fix the problem, and **tell its users**.

## Key Points

1. **The registry won't let you revert to deprecated models** like `claude-legacy` — attempting to do so returns `REG-1010` error.

2. **Pause the agent**: Use `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` with `"status": "paused"` to stop new sessions from starting. As documented in the Registry API reference ([D01:5]), setting status to `paused` stops new sessions from starting, while `retired` hides the agent from listings.

3. **Notify your users**: Inform stakeholders immediately about the outage and expected downtime.

4. **Fix the issue before unpausing**: Once the underlying problem is resolved, you may be able to migrate to a different target model or adjust configurations. Remember, model changes take effect on the agent's next session, not in the middle of running ones ([D07:4]).

## Example Command

To pause an agent during troubleshooting:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/research_agent \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -d '{"status": "paused"}'
```

## Important Note
If you need to restore the agent to functionality, you would only be able to move it to another non-deprecated model. There's no mechanism in the registry to simply revert to the previous model if it has been deprecated.

Based on the company runbooks and documentation, here's how to handle a model migration rollback when the new model misbehaves:

## What Happens When a Model Migrations Goes Wrong

According to the [Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy]([D07:5]):

> **You can't roll back to `claude-legacy`: the registry refuses it.** If the new model misbehaves, **set the agent's `status` to `paused`** while you fix the problem, and **tell its users**.

## Key Points

1. **The registry won't let you revert to deprecated models** like `claude-legacy` — attempting to do so returns `REG-1010` error.

2. **Pause the agent**: Use `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` with `"status": "paused"` to stop new sessions from starting. As documented in the Registry API reference ([D01:5]), setting status to `paused` stops new sessions from starting, while `retired` hides the agent from listings.

3. **Notify your users**: Inform stakeholders immediately about the outage and expected downtime.

4. **Fix the issue before unpausing**: Once the underlying problem is resolved, you may be able to migrate to a different target model or adjust configurations. Remember, model changes take effect on the agent's next session, not in the middle of running ones ([D07:4]).

## Example Command

To pause an agent during troubleshooting:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/research_agent \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -d '{"status": "paused"}'
```

## Important Note
If you need to restore the agent to functionality, you would only be able to move it to another non-deprecated model. There's no mechanism in the registry to simply revert to the previous model if it has been deprecated.

## What Happens When a Model Migrations Goes Wrong

According to the [Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy]([D07:5]):

> **You can't roll back to `claude-legacy`: the registry refuses it.** If the new model misbehaves, **set the agent's `status` to `paused`** while you fix the problem, and **tell its users**.

3. **Notify your users**: Inform stakeholders immediately about the outage and expected downtime.

4. **Fix the issue before unpausing**: Once the underlying problem is resolved, you may be able to migrate to a different target model or adjust configurations. Remember, model changes take effect on the agent's next session, not in the middle of running ones ([D07:4]).

## Example Command

```bash

Based on my search of the registry documentation, I don't find explicit runbook procedures specifically for rolling back model migrations. However, the procedure is straightforward - you simply revert the model back to its previous value using the registry API.

Here's how to rollback a model migration:

**Method 1: Using the Registry API (recommended)**

Use the `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` endpoint to set the agent back to its previous model:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/{agent_id} \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{previous_model_name}"}'
```

**Method 2: Direct tool call**

If you're using the internal tools, you can call the `set_model` function directly:
```
set_model(agent_name="{agent_id}", model="{previous_model}")
```

**Important notes:**

1. **The change applies from the agent's next session** - currently running sessions will continue with the misbehaving model until they end [D01:5]

2. **Model must be allowed on the agent's tier** - if the new model isn't on your agent's tier allowlist, the update will fail with error `REG-1007`. You may need to adjust the tier first [D01:4]

3. **Check agent health first** - before committing to a rollback, verify which agent is affected and check its current health metrics. Use the `get_health` tool or look at the monitoring dashboard to confirm performance issues [D08:0]

4. **Monitor recovery** - after the rollback, watch the agent's p95 response time and error rate in the dashboards to confirm the issue has resolved

If you'd like help identifying a specific agent that needs rollbacking, I can check its status and current model configuration for you.

<source id="D01:5" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Updating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Updating an agent

`PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` changes one or more of `model`, `tier`, `owner` and `status`. Send only the fields you're changing. It needs a `write` key; a `read` key gets `REG-1004`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/research_agent \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "claude-sonnet"}'
```

A change takes effect on the agent's next session, not in the middle of one that's running. Setting `status` to `paused` stops new sessions from starting; `retired` also hides the agent from the default listing.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D01:0" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Overview" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Overview

The Registry API stores the configuration of every agent the company runs: its name, the model it uses, its tier, its owner and its status. Agents and internal tools read it to find out how an agent is configured, and owners write to it to change that configuration. The current version is v2.6.

All endpoints live under one base URL:

```
https://registry.internal.example/v2
```

Requests and responses are JSON. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.
</source>

## Dashboards

Each agent has a panel with latency, error rate and sessions. The overview dashboard shows every active agent on one screen, sorted by p95. Panels refresh every 30 seconds and lag real time by up to a minute.
</source>

<source id="D08:0" doc="D08" title="Monitoring guide" section="Monitoring guide > What monitoring collects" date="2026-03-02" type="official">
## What monitoring collects

For every agent, monitoring records response time (as p50 and p95), error rate, and the number of sessions. It learns which agents exist by asking the registry for the agent list every 30 seconds, so a new agent appears on the dashboards within a minute of being created.
</source>

<source id="D01:8" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Rate limits" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Rate limits

Each key may make 60 requests per minute. Requests past the limit get HTTP 429 with error `REG-1009` and a `Retry-After` header giving the number of seconds to wait. Limits apply per key, not per agent, so two processes sharing one key share one limit.
</source>

Based on my search of the registry documentation, I don't find explicit runbook procedures specifically for rolling back model migrations. However, the procedure is straightforward - you simply revert the model back to its previous value using the registry API.

Here's how to rollback a model migration:

**Method 1: Using the Registry API (recommended)**

Use the `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` endpoint to set the agent back to its previous model:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/{agent_id} \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{previous_model_name}"}'
```

**Method 2: Direct tool call**

If you're using the internal tools, you can call the `set_model` function directly:
```
set_model(agent_name="{agent_id}", model="{previous_model}")
```

**Important notes:**

1. **The change applies from the agent's next session** - currently running sessions will continue with the misbehaving model until they end [D01:5]

2. **Model must be allowed on the agent's tier** - if the new model isn't on your agent's tier allowlist, the update will fail with error `REG-1007`. You may need to adjust the tier first [D01:4]

3. **Check agent health first** - before committing to a rollback, verify which agent is affected and check its current health metrics. Use the `get_health` tool or look at the monitoring dashboard to confirm performance issues [D08:0]

4. **Monitor recovery** - after the rollback, watch the agent's p95 response time and error rate in the dashboards to confirm the issue has resolved

If you'd like help identifying a specific agent that needs rollbacking, I can check its status and current model configuration for you.

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

Based on my search of the registry documentation, I don't find explicit runbook procedures specifically for rolling back model migrations. However, the procedure is straightforward - you simply revert the model back to its previous value using the registry API.

Here's how to rollback a model migration:

**Method 1: Using the Registry API (recommended)**

Use the `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` endpoint to set the agent back to its previous model:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/{agent_id} \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "{previous_model_name}"}'
```

**Method 2: Direct tool call**

If you're using the internal tools, you can call the `set_model` function directly:
```
set_model(agent_name="{agent_id}", model="{previous_model}")
```

**Important notes:**

1. **The change applies from the agent's next session** - currently running sessions will continue with the misbehaving model until they end [D01:5]

2. **Model must be allowed on the agent's tier** - if the new model isn't on your agent's tier allowlist, the update will fail with error `REG-1007`. You may need to adjust the tier first [D01:4]

3. **Check agent health first** - before committing to a rollback, verify which agent is affected and check its current health metrics. Use the `get_health` tool or look at the monitoring dashboard to confirm performance issues [D08:0]

4. **Monitor recovery** - after the rollback, watch the agent's p95 response time and error rate in the dashboards to confirm the issue has resolved

Based on the company documentation, here's how to check that a new registry key deployment works:

## Verification Step (from Runbook: rotating a registry key [D06:3])

From the agent's environment, call `GET /agents/me` with your new key:

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $YOUR_NEW_KEY"
```

**What to expect:**
- ✅ **Success**: The response should return the agent you rotated (not an error code)
- ❌ **Error REG-1002** (`INVALID_KEY`): The secret holds a truncated or mistyped key
- ❌ **Error REG-1001** (`MISSING_KEY`): No `X-Registry-Key` header was sent

The registry requires authentication via the `X-Registry-Key` header on every request. A read-only key can verify your agent identity by calling `/agents/me`.

**Note**: If you're experiencing other issues after key rotation, check error codes like:
- `REG-1003` (`KEY_REVOKED`) - Some process is still holding the old key
- `REG-1004` (`FORBIDDEN_FIELD`) - Key scope doesn't allow this change

## Registry key errors

If an agent starts getting `REG-1003` after a key rotation, some process is still holding the old key. Usually it's a cron job or a second deployment nobody remembered. Search the secrets manager for the old key id. <source id="D02:0" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Authentication errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1001` | `MISSING_KEY` | 401 | The request had no `X-Registry-Key` header. |
| `REG-1002` | `INVALID_KEY` | 401 | The key isn't one the registry issued. Check for a truncated or mistyped key. |
| `REG-1003` | `KEY_REVOKED` | 401 | The key was valid but has been revoked. Issue a new key; a revoked key can't be restored. |
| `REG-1004` | `FORBIDDEN_FIELD` | 403 | The key's scope doesn't allow this change. Writes need a `write` key. |
</source>

<source id="D05:4" doc="D05" title="Runbook: agent latency spike" section="Runbook: agent latency spike > Step 4: Check for rate limiting" date="2026-07-09" type="official">
## Step 4: Check for rate limiting

Look for `REG-1009` responses in the agent's logs. An agent that's being rate-limited waits for `Retry-After` on every call, which looks like latency. If you find them, check whether another process is sharing the agent's key.
</source>

<source id="D01:1" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Authentication" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication

Every request must carry a registry key in the `X-Registry-Key` header. A request without one is rejected with `REG-1001`, and a key the registry doesn't recognise is rejected with `REG-1002`.

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY"
```

Keys have a scope. A `read` key can call every `GET` endpoint. A `write` key can also create, update and delete agents. Each key belongs to exactly one agent or one person, and the registry records which one made every change. Keys are issued and revoked with `regctl`; see the key rotation runbook.
</source>

## Step 4: Check for rate limiting

<source id="D01:1" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Authentication" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication

Every request must carry a registry key in the `X-Registry-Key` header. A request without one is rejected with `REG-1001`, and a key the registry doesn't recognise is rejected with `REG-1002`.

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY"
```

Keys have a scope. A `read` key can call every `GET` endpoint. A `write` key can also create, update and delete agents. Each key belongs to exactly one agent or one person, and the registry records which one made every change. Keys are issued and revoked with `regctl`; see the key rotation runbook.
</source>

**Step 1: Call the agent's own endpoint**

curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \

answers:
Based on the registry key rotation runbook, here's how to verify a newly deployed registry key works:

## Verification Step

**Call `GET /agents/me` with the new key** from the agent's environment. This is the quickest way to confirm the deployment worked.

If successful, you'll get the agent record (e.g., agent_id, model, tier, owner, status). [D01:3]

**Expected result:** The agent details you just rotated.

**Error cases:**
- `REG-1002` (INVALID_KEY): The secret holds a truncated or mistyped key. Check your secrets manager entry. [D02:0]
- `REG-1001` (MISSING_KEY): The request lacked the `X-Registry-Key` header entirely. [D01:1]

## Example Test Command

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $NEW_REGISTRY_KEY"
```

## Additional Checks

After verifying the key works, you may also want to:
- Check that old sessions eventually pick up the new key (new sessions use it immediately; running sessions finish on the old one) [D06:2]
- Monitor for `REG-1003` errors, which would indicate something missed in deployment [D06:4]

## Deployment Order

The complete process is:
1. **Issue the new key** with `regctl keys issue --agent <agent_id> --scope write`
2. **Deploy it** by updating the agent's secret and redeploying
3. **Verify** using `GET /agents/me` 
4. **Revoke the old key** within 24 hours [D06:4]

## When to rotate

Rotate an agent's registry key every 90 days, and immediately if the key may have been exposed: written to a log, pasted in a chat, or committed to a repository. An exposed key is rotated first and investigated second.
</source>

- This incident is why the key rotation runbook says to rotate first and investigate second.
</source>

Based on the registry key rotation runbook, here's how to verify a newly deployed registry key works:

## Verification Step

**Call `GET /agents/me` with the new key** from the agent's environment. This is the quickest way to confirm the deployment worked.

If successful, you'll get the agent record (e.g., agent_id, model, tier, owner, status). [D01:3]

**Expected result:** The agent details you just rotated.

**Error cases:**
- `REG-1002` (INVALID_KEY): The secret holds a truncated or mistyped key. Check your secrets manager entry. [D02:0]
- `REG-1001` (MISSING_KEY): The request lacked the `X-Registry-Key` header entirely. [D01:1]

## Example Test Command

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $NEW_REGISTRY_KEY"
```

## Additional Checks

After verifying the key works, you may also want to:
- Check that old sessions eventually pick up the new key (new sessions use it immediately; running sessions finish on the old one) [D06:2]
- Monitor for `REG-1003` errors, which would indicate something missed in deployment [D06:4]

## Deployment Order

The complete process is:
1. **Issue the new key** with `regctl keys issue --agent <agent_id> --scope write`
2. **Deploy it** by updating the agent's secret and redeploying
3. **Verify** using `GET /agents/me` 
4. **Revoke the old key** within 24 hours [D06:4]

Based on the company documentation:

**Models a standard-tier agent can use:**
- `claude-haiku`
- `claude-sonnet`

This is defined in the registry's "Tiers and models" section [D01:7].

**What happens if you assign an unallowed model:**
If you try to change a standard-tier agent to a model not on its allowlist (like `claude-opus` or `claude-legacy`), the request will **fail with error code `REG-1007`**, which means "MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED" [D02:1]. The specific error message will indicate that the model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier.

To fix this, you have two options:
1. Change the agent's tier to `priority` (which allows `claude-opus`) first
2. Pick an allowed model like `claude-haiku` or `claude-sonnet`

Note: `claude-legacy` is deprecated and cannot be assigned to any new agents [D01:7].

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

## Delay `__name__` label removal for PromQL engine

Note that evaluating parts of the query separately will still trigger the
labelset collision. This commonly happens when analyzing intermediate results
of a query manually or with a tool like PromLens.

If a query refers to the already removed `__name__` label, its behavior may
change while this feature flag is set. (Example: `sum by (__name__)
(rate({foo="bar"}[5m]))`, see details on
GitHub.)
These queries are rare to occur and easy to fix. (In the above example,
removing `by (__name__)` doesn't change anything without the feature flag and
fixes the possible problem with the feature flag.)
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/guides/contributing.md:14" doc="prometheus-docs/guides/contributing.md" title="Contributing" section="Contributing > GitHub guidelines" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## GitHub guidelines

Once you have a change you would like to propose, push it to your personal fork 
of Prometheus and open a pull request against the default branch. The default 
branch is usually `main` but can be `master` in some repositories.
Some situations require a PR against a release branch, e.g. `release-3.5`. The 
most common situations are fixes for a release candidate for a new release or a 
fix for an LTS version of Prometheus. If in doubt, ask via one of the channels 
mentioned in this document.

The needed reviewers will be added automatically. Anyone else that should or 
wants to review a change can be mentioned by their user name in a comment, but 
please avoid pinging random community members.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-server/migration.md:21" doc="prometheus-server/migration.md" title="Prometheus 3.0 migration guide" section="Prometheus 3.0 migration guide > Miscellaneous > `le` and `quantile` label values" date="2026-09-26" type="vendor">
### `le` and `quantile` label values

`my_classic_hist{le="1.0"}` being ingested into prometheus, no matter via which
protocol. The effect of this change is that alerts, recording rules and
dashboards that directly reference label values as whole numbers such as
`le="1"` will stop working.

Ways to deal with this change either globally or on a per metric basis:

- Fix references to integer `le`, `quantile` label values, but otherwise do
nothing and accept that some queries that span the transition time will produce
inaccurate or unexpected results.
_This is the recommended solution._
- Use `metric_relabel_config` to retain the old labels when scraping targets.
This should **only** be applied to metrics that currently produce such labels.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/guides/contributing.md:13" doc="prometheus-docs/guides/contributing.md" title="Contributing" section="Contributing > GitHub guidelines" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## GitHub guidelines

Commit messages should describe the change made in the commit.
We don't have strong opinions on how large or small commits should be, use your 
best judgment to make a logical series of changes. Good commits make reviews 
easier and thus can be merged faster. For example it's a good pattern to have a 
commit adding a test to expose a bug and then have a separate commit to fix the 
bug.
Commit messages must include a `Signed-off-by: <author identity>` line. With 
this the author agrees to the terms published at 
https://developercertificate.org/ for _that_ particular contribution.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="alertmanager/high_availability.md:22" doc="alertmanager/high_availability.md" title="High Availability" section="High Availability > Silence Management in HA > Silence Expiry" date="2026-09-27" type="vendor">
### Silence Expiry

Silences have:
- `StartsAt`, `EndsAt` - The active time range
- `ExpiresAt` - When to garbage collect (EndsAt + retention period)
- `UpdatedAt` - For conflict resolution during merge

Each instance independently:
- Evaluates silence state (pending/active/expired) based on current time
- Garbage collects expired silences past their retention period
- The GC is local only (no gossip) since all instances converge to the same decision
</source>

<source id="D09:1" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Timeline" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Timeline

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/guides/multi-target-exporter.md:22" doc="prometheus-docs/guides/multi-target-exporter.md" title="Understanding and using the multi-target exporter pattern" section="Understanding and using the multi-target exporter pattern > Configuring modules" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## Configuring modules

You can see that the probe was successful and get many useful metrics, like latency by phase, status code, ssl status or certificate expiry in Unix time.
The blackbox exporter also offers a tiny web interface at localhost:9115 for you to check out the last few probes, the loaded config and debug information. It even offers a direct link to probe `prometheus.io`. Handy if you are wondering why something does not work.
</source>

<source id="D09:0" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Summary" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Summary

On 2026-04-08, `billing_agent` failed to issue invoices for 2 hours 15 minutes. Every attempt ended in a timeout from payments-gateway. No customer was charged twice, but 1,140 invoices went out late.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="alertmanager/high_availability.md:22" doc="alertmanager/high_availability.md" title="High Availability" section="High Availability > Silence Management in HA > Silence Expiry" date="2026-09-27" type="vendor">
### Silence Expiry

Silences have:
- `StartsAt`, `EndsAt` - The active time range
- `ExpiresAt` - When to garbage collect (EndsAt + retention period)
- `UpdatedAt` - For conflict resolution during merge

Each instance independently:
- Evaluates silence state (pending/active/expired) based on current time
- Garbage collects expired silences past their retention period
- The GC is local only (no gossip) since all instances converge to the same decision
</source>

<source id="D09:1" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Timeline" date="2026-04-10" type="official">

</source>

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D13:0" doc="D13" title="billing_agent spend limits and approvals" section="billing_agent spend limits and approvals > Monthly limit" date="2026-09-01" type="official">
## Monthly limit

`billing_agent`'s model usage is capped at $4,000 per calendar month. At 80% of the cap, the Finance operations lead gets an email. At 100%, `billing_agent` is set to `paused` until the next month or until the cap is raised.
</source>

### `le` and `quantile` label values

`my_classic_hist{le="1.0"}` being ingested into prometheus, no matter via which
protocol. The effect of this change is that alerts, recording rules and
dashboards that directly reference label values as whole numbers such as
`le="1"` will stop working.

Ways to deal with this change either globally or on a per metric basis:

- Fix references to integer `le`, `quantile` label values, but otherwise do
nothing and accept that some queries that span the transition time will produce
inaccurate or unexpected results.
_This is the recommended solution._
- Use `metric_relabel_config` to retain the old labels when scraping targets.
This should **only** be applied to metrics that currently produce such labels.
</source>

## Bucketing

However, picking the right buckets in advance can be challenging. And changing
buckets later creates a lot of disruption (as you will see below). If you
instrument code directly with native histograms, you do not pick any bucket
boundaries explicitly, but you configure a desired resolution. Buckets are
created dynamically following an exponential bucketing schema, covering the
whole range of floating point numbers from -Inf to +Inf. Higher resolution
causes higher resource usage, but generally you can reach much higher resolution
than with classic histograms for the same resource cost. Instrumentation
libraries also offer various strategies to limit the count of populated
buckets, like occasional resets of the histogram or adaptive resolution
</source>

<source id="D01:7" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Tiers and models" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Tiers and models

Every agent has a tier, and each tier allows a fixed set of models:

| Tier | Allowed models |
|---|---|
| `standard` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet` |
| `priority` | `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet`, `claude-opus` |

Moving an agent to `claude-opus` therefore means moving it to the `priority` tier first, which needs approval from its owner's budget holder. `claude-legacy` is deprecated and can't be assigned to any agent; existing agents on it keep working until 2026-10-31.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D14:1" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > Can my agent use the biggest model?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## Can my agent use the biggest model?

Only on the priority tier. Standard-tier agents can use the smaller and mid-sized models. Moving to priority needs a sign-off from whoever holds your team's budget, and after that you can change the model.
</source>

## Per-step stats

- **totalQueryableSamples** / **totalQueryableSamplesPerStep**: Total number of samples *loaded* during the query. For range-vector functions (e.g. `rate`, `sum_over_time`) evaluated over multiple steps, each step counts the full window (the same point may be counted in multiple steps).
- **samplesRead** / **samplesReadPerStep**: Total number of samples *read* (I/O). For range-vector functions in range queries, only *new* points per step are counted (step 0: full window; later steps: points not seen in the previous step). For other query types, this equals totalQueryableSamples.
- **peakSamples**: Peak number of samples in memory during evaluation (used for the `query.max-samples` limit).
</source>

## Defining alerting rules

The optional `for` clause causes Prometheus to wait for a certain duration
between first encountering a new expression output vector element and counting
an alert as firing for this element. In this case, Prometheus will check that
the alert continues to be active during each evaluation for 10 minutes before

## Per-step stats

- **totalQueryableSamples** / **totalQueryableSamplesPerStep**: Total number of samples *loaded* during the query. For range-vector functions (e.g. `rate`, `sum_over_time`) evaluated over multiple steps, each step counts the full window (the same point may be counted in multiple steps).
- **samplesRead** / **samplesReadPerStep**: Total number of samples *read* (I/O). For range-vector functions in range queries, only *new* points per step are counted (step 0: full window; later steps: points not seen in the previous step). For other query types, this equals totalQueryableSamples.
- **peakSamples**: Peak number of samples in memory during evaluation (used for the `query.max-samples` limit).
</source>

## Per-step stats

- **totalQueryableSamples** / **totalQueryableSamplesPerStep**: Total number of samples *loaded* during the query. For range-vector functions (e.g. `rate`, `sum_over_time`) evaluated over multiple steps, each step counts the full window (the same point may be counted in multiple steps).
- **samplesRead** / **samplesReadPerStep**: Total number of samples *read* (I/O). For range-vector functions in range queries, only *new* points per step are counted (step 0: full window; later steps: points not seen in the previous step). For other query types, this equals totalQueryableSamples.
- **peakSamples**: Peak number of samples in memory during evaluation (used for the `query.max-samples` limit).
</source>

<source id="D10:0" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > Summary" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## Summary

From 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-22, `research_agent` answered questions with knowledge-base articles that had since been updated. Nothing failed and no alert fired; a user noticed that a report quoted a policy that had changed four days earlier.
</source>

<source id="D10:2" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > Why it took a week to notice" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## Why it took a week to notice

The agent's latency and error rate looked better than usual: cached answers are fast and never fail. Nothing in monitoring measures whether results are current. The only signal was a person comparing an answer with the source.
</source>

<source id="D10:1" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What happened" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

### `batch_send_deadline`

Batch send deadline sets the maximum amount of time between sends for a single
shard. Even if the queued shards has not reached `max_samples_per_send`, a
request will be sent. Batch send deadline can be increased for low volume
systems that are not latency sensitive in order to increase request efficiency.
</source>

<source id="D01:5" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Updating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Updating an agent

`PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` changes one or more of `model`, `tier`, `owner` and `status`. Send only the fields you're changing. It needs a `write` key; a `read` key gets `REG-1004`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/research_agent \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "claude-sonnet"}'
```

A change takes effect on the agent's next session, not in the middle of one that's running. Setting `status` to `paused` stops new sessions from starting; `retired` also hides the agent from the default listing.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">

- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

Batch send deadline sets the maximum amount of time between sends for a single

</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
